+# ADR 0001: Increase Pricing Cache TTL
+
+**Date:** 2026-07-24  
+**Status:** Accepted
+
+## Context
+
+Our pricing data endpoint is a critical service dependency that experiences consistent traffic patterns throughout the day. Currently, we cache pricing information with a TTL of 900 seconds (15 minutes), which results in frequent cache misses and repeated backend lookups during peak usage periods. Analysis of our pricing data shows that changes are released in scheduled batches, typically once per day, with minimal real-time updates required between releases.
+
+The backend pricing service has throughput constraints and experiences degraded response times when handling the volume of cache-miss requests during peak hours. Our monitoring data indicates that pricing changes propagate within a 1-hour window following a release, making the current 15-minute TTL more aggressive than necessary for business requirements.
+
+## Decision
+
+We have decided to increase the pricing cache TTL from 900 seconds (15 minutes) to 3600 seconds (1 hour). This change aligns the cache duration with our actual pricing update cycles and reduces unnecessary backend load during peak traffic periods. The extended TTL still provides sufficient freshness for pricing consistency while significantly improving system efficiency.
+
+This decision applies to the pricing cache layer across all services that depend on pricing data. The change is transparent to consumers of pricing information and requires no API contract modifications.
+
+## Consequences
+
+**Positive:** Cache hit rates will increase by an estimated 60–70%, reducing backend load during peak hours and improving overall API response latency. This reduces strain on the pricing service infrastructure and decreases operational costs. The predictable cache window aligns with our release schedule, making cache invalidation at release time a reliable strategy.
+
+**Negative:** Pricing information will be stale for up to 1 hour after a release in the worst case, though typically propagation is much faster. Clients who require real-time pricing updates will need to implement cache bypass mechanisms (e.g., cache-busting headers) or query a separate low-latency endpoint. Teams deploying pricing changes must coordinate with the cache invalidation process to avoid serving outdated prices.
+
+**Mitigation:** We will implement a cache invalidation endpoint that allows manual purging when pricing releases are deployed, reducing the stale-data window to seconds. Monitoring and alerting will track cache staleness and alert ops teams to pricing mismatches.
